messages.author: 7fcc0cf58f9078b8
messages.subject: Detection history by hour
parts:
Hi!

It is possible to get a detection history by hour? I understand that occasionLength is the occupation period (day or days) but this only accepts integers. I did read camtrapR´s PDF and vignettes but I did not find anything about that. Do you know any way to get this?

This is the script I am using to get my detection history:

hist_captura <- cameraOperation(CTtable = reserva_camaras,
  stationCol = "Station",
  setupCol = "Fecha_colocación",
  retrievalCol = "Fecha_retiro",
  hasProblems = T,
  dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y")

ocu_canis_hourly <- detectionHistory(
  recordTable = registros_reserva,                
  camOp = hist_captura, 
  stationCo = "Station",
  speciesCol = "Species",
  recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
  recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d",
  species = "Canis lupus familiaris", 
  occasionLength = 1, 
  day1 = "station", 
  includeEffort = FALSE,
  timeZone = "America/Mexico_City")

Thank you for your responses
I apologize for my English, it is not my first language!

messages.author: bd00314644d53a96
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Detection history by hour
parts:
Hi Mariano,

Currently I believe that CamtrapR's base functions do not create hour detection histories. However, you can use the custom function developed by Fabiola Iannarilli in her paper Using lorelograms to measure and model correlation in binary data: Applications to ecological studies . All the codes and data they used are open and hosted at: https://conservancy.umn.edu/handle/11299/208294  
Just download the zip of the data and use the function in the script called "Modified_function_for_detection_histories_by_hour.R"
The arguments are based on the original camtrapR function so it is not that difficult to use. However, if you have a very long sampling (more than 30 days) you will have a huge detection matrix. So sometimes it is useful to make a subset.
I hope you find it helpful.

Best regards,

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Detection history by hour
parts:
Hi, 
as Gabriel said, currently that is not implemented in camtrapR. The link shared above might indeed help though. 
There may also be alternative ways to create such detection histories manually, e.g. with the help of the lubridate package. You could for every record extract the date and hour and construct, convert each of those to a number (e.g. hours since beginning of study), and make a detection history based on that. 

In camtrapR, it might be quite a bit of work to adapt detectionHistory to return hourly detection (due to how the function is integrated with cameraOperation, which uses days). So it would be a major project that I unfortunately don't have the time for at the moment. 

Best regards,
Jürgen
